Towards the end of his life, he was occupied with verse from the Middle Ages, and in particular with Charlemagne and Harun al-Rashid. He produced scholarship on Romanesque poetry and on the literary works of Heinrich Heine.

title: FIDE World Cup of Rapid Chess
text: The tournament began with a preliminary group stage (21-22 March), where the sixteen players were split into two groups of eight players each. Each group played a seven-game round robin, with the top four players from each advancing to an eight-player single-elimination knockout (23-25 March) to determine the champion. Each knockout match was best-of-two games with alternating colors. In case of a tie, the players would play two 5-minute blitz games, also with alternating colors. If still tied, a sudden-death armageddon game, with 6 minutes for White versus 5 minutes for Black, would determine who advances.

title: Selected Stories (Robert Walser short story collection)
text: The selections date from about 1905 to the mid 1920's, and most pieces were previously published in German in periodicals during Walser's lifetime. Scholar and translator Christopher Middleton stated that the selection aims to present some of the "main lines, or radiations, of [Walser's] power of invention in the miniature, of his charm in the grotesque, also of his ironic reflexivity, [...] his jazzy oscillations between levels of discourse--dense and transparent, straight and mocking." Middleton has said that Walser excelled in the field of short prose and that he was "at its best in miniature fictions with a rapid pulse, [...] sketches, soliloquies, improvisations, arabesques, and capriccios."

title: Selected Stories (Robert Walser short story collection)
text: [...]A Paul Klee in prose--as delicate, as sly, as haunted. [...] Walser's [work is] charged with compassion: awareness of the creatureliness of life, of the fellowship of sadness. [...] As literature's present [...] remakes its past, we cannot help but see Walser as the missing link between Kleist and Kafka, who admired him greatly. [...] At the time [of Walser's writing], it was more likely to be Kafka [who was understood] through the prism of Walser. Robert Musil, another admirer among Walser's contemporaries, when he first read Kafka pronounced [him] "a peculiar case of the Walser type." The moral core of Walser's art is the refusal of power; of domination. [...] Walser's virtues are those of the most mature, most civilized art. He is truly a wonderful, heartbreaking writer."

title: Fortifications of Westerplatte
text: The Polish were granted access to the Westerplatte Peninsula by the League of Nations in 1924 to build a military transit depot (WST). Some of the conditions of granting the peninsula to the Polish were that they could not have more than 88 military personnel, and build fortifications. The peninsula was separated from the Free City of Danzig by a 2m tall brick wall that ran across the base of the peninsula. In the summer of 1933, Polish authorities decided to secretly begin building fortifications on the peninsula as the threat of German aggression became more real. The first fortifications were several concrete blockhouses, light shelters, and gun emplacements.

title: Prefabricated building, Keilor Park
text: In 1840 William Taylor, a pioneer Scottish-born pastoralist, arrived in the District of Port Phillip in the company of Dugald McPherson and together they took up several pastoral runs in the Wimmera region. In 1849, Taylor established another pastoral run at Overnewton on the Salt Water River, close to the ford crossing. A small settlement including one of the first inns erected in the district grew up in an ad hoc manner at this crossing place. The village of Keilor was gazetted as a township in 1850 and, during the Victorian gold rush period, thousands of diggers used the crossing place on the Salt Water River at Keilor on their way to the Central Victorian goldfields. The infant township burgeoned in the 1850s and agriculturists set up small farms on the alluvial flats to provide fresh produce to the miners. Many of the first settlers were Irish immigrants who had fled Ireland after the potato famine of 1846 or who were later attracted to the Victorian colony by the prospect of striking it rich on the Victorian goldfields.

title: Prefabricated building, Keilor Park
text: The Old Colonial-style cottage is rectangular in plan with external walls and arch roof of galvanised corrugated wrought iron, with a thirteen-centimetre (five-inch) pitch. The structural frame comprises horizontal wrought iron angle top and bottom plates bolted to vertical cast iron corner angles and intermediate supports. The cast iron pilasters have slightly recessed panels terminating in semicircular arches. The interior is lightly framed in timber to take the windows and a timber or fabric lining. Internally there are large hand painted numerals on various components likely to have aided in assembly. The framing, windows, and two fireplace openings indicate that the building was probably used for residential purposes.

title: I Wrote You a Letter
text: The release of M83's previous album, Fantasy, in 2023, marked the debut of Gonzalez's independent music label, named Other Suns, powered by Believe Music. This label would later receive a couple of soundtracks composed by M83 (namely A Necessary Escape, for the 2025 film Dakar: Race Against the Desert, and Resurrection, for the homonymous film directed by Bi Gan), while also hosting studio albums of artists associated with the band, including Kaela Sinclair's Supraliminal and Benoît de Villeneuve's Soul Tuning, both in 2025. Concurrently, with M83's ninth studio album released, Gonzalez held an artistic priority of touring throughout North America and Europe, and with the conclusion of the shows, he began producing the aforementioned soundtracks and the next full-length album in 2024, in the continued vision of making cinematic soundscapes for "people to go on big adventures, to feel alive and to forget about the world", as he said in an interview by Clash Music about Fantasy.

title: Avinash Raghudevan
text: Early in his career, Avinash is known for the film Jil Jung Juk (2016), directed by Deeraj Vaidy, in which he starred alongside Siddharth and Sananth. Avinash has stated that he improvises when portraying his characters. However, after the film's release, both its critical reception and box-office performance were lackluster. Avinash's performance in the film received acclaim. Subsequently, he played supporting roles in several films, such as Sethum Aayiram Pon (2020), Fight Club (2023), Retro (2025), 29 (2026), and DC (2026). Notably, his performances in Fight Club, 29, and DC once again garnered praise from film critics.

title: Little Girl (John Lennon song)
text: "Little Girl" was recorded sometime in 1965 at John Lennon's home at the time, and dates to around the same time as "Day Tripper". The sixty year old demo never circulated on any bootleg and was never traded amongst collectors. Very few people knew of its existence, not even the band's biggest fans, until the Rubber Soul: Special Edition box set was announced in 2026. According to Kevin Howlett, EMI archivist Allan Rouse was the first person outside of the Lennon Estate, with a few other people who worked at Abbey Road, to have known about it. Giles Martin, who produced the set, only found out about the demo when Sean Lennon gave a tape reel from his father's archives and telling him "Oh, and then there's this."

title: Lammert Huitema
text: He began ice skating at the age of ten and was part of the Groningen junior squad. As a teenager, he had to undergo knee surgery owing to overuse. He could not skate for the next four years. His doctor advised him to take up cycling. He began his career as an eighteen-year-old cyclist in 1980 and started racing at the amateur level in 1982. In May 1982, he won a race in Wolfsburg, Germany, by a wide margin. He twice won the criterium in his hometown of Roden. He resumed speed skating in 1984, combining it with cycling. He achieved his first speed skating victory as a B-category skater on 23 December 1986, at the Stadspark Groningen artificial ice rink. He also competed in long-track races and won the 500 metres at the Groningen championships in January 1987. In late January 1987, he became the Groningen marathon champion in the B and C categories.

title: Lammert Huitema
text: Starting in the 1988/1989 season, he competed in the A-division, though the step up proved significant during that first year. He achieved his first victory at the top level in December 1989 at the Assen marathon (held at De Bonte Wever), which counted towards the KNSB Cup. He finished fourth in the final standings of the KNSB Cup as a newcomer. During the summer of 1990, he also competed as a cyclist in criteriums, winning the race in his birthplace, Haren. However, for him, cycling was secondary to marathon speed skating. In December 1990, he surprised all the top skaters by snatching the victory in the marathon at De Meent in Alkmaar. Huitema was also the fastest in the first natural-ice marathon in Veenoord, Drenthe, on 3 February 1991.

title: Lammert Huitema
text: The best period of Huitema's career began around his thirtieth birthday in 1991. At the Dutch artificial-ice marathon skating championships held at the Eindhoven ice rink on 12 January 1991, he lost the sprint to Richard van Kempen, finishing second. Although he preferred not to skate on natural ice, he reached the podium twice in natural-ice classics that year. After winning bronze in the 100 van Eernewoude on 12 February he took silver in the Noordwesthoekrit two days later. Yep Kramer was the winner on both occasions. Huitema participated in an Alternative Elfstedentocht for the first time on 11 March 1991. He finished third in Rovaniemi, Finland, in the 200-kilometre race won by Evert van Benthem. He repeated this feat a year later, also in Rovaniemi. At the KNSB Cup in late February 1992, he reached the final podium for the first time by finishing third. Huitema won, among other events, the marathon at Thialf in Heerenveen.

title: Sławomir Pietrzyk
text: In the 2010 Polish local elections, he ran from the same committee again, winning 1,697 (5.32%) votes and reclaiming his mandate. He became a close associate of the incumbent mayor Jacek Majchrowski, and was nominated the Vice-Chairman of the city council in 2010. As the Vice-Chairman, he suspended his membership in Social Democracy of Poland and became a member of political association Friendly Kraków (Polish: Przyjazny Kraków), which entered a coalition with the Civic Platform. He ran for re-election in the 2014 and 2018 local elections, winning 1,288 (4.58%) and 1,774 (4.53%) votes respectively and maintaining his seat. In 2018, Gazeta Wyborcza described Pietrzyk as the left wing of mayor Majchrowski's movement, sympathetic to the Democratic Left Alliance.

title: Sławomir Pietrzyk
text: On 6 December 2021, Kraków City Council from the Civic Platform, Alicja Szczepańska, filed a formal complaint about Pietrzyk. She alleged that during a formal meeting with a Lwów delegation, Pietrzyk offered to have a sexual intercourse with her, and later encouraged her to have sexual relations with one of the Lwów deputies. On 10 January 2022, the Disciplinary Committee voted to remove Pietrzyk from the role of Vice-Chairman. Pietrzyk strongly rejected the allegations, arguing that he fell victim to political intrigue. Despite losing his position as Vice-Chairman, he remained a city council member for the rest of his term.

title: Sławomir Pietrzyk
text: On 2 June 2026, he announced his candidacy for the 2026 Kraków mayoral election, and was endorsed by Social Democracy of Poland. He was subsequently also endorsed by Joanna Senyszyn, the founder of New Wave party who became famous for her 2025 Polish presidential election run. He campaigned on issues affecting elderly citizens of Kraków, and made ambitious political promises, such as making the Kraków public transport free. The media ignored his candidacy, and in one public debate, only six seats were prepared, leaving Pietrzyk, the seventh candidate, unable to participate. Ultimately, he won 947 (0.37%) votes, finishing last. He expressed disappointment at his performance. At the same time, he stated his readiness to endorse one of the runoff candidates, although ultimately he remained undecided.

title: RKO Bushwick Theatre
text: In April 1912 the Bushwick Theatre was acquired by theatre magnate Benjamin Franklin Keith, and became a part of the Keith Circuit of vaudeville theatres. By the following July it had been rebranded B. F. Keith's Bushwick Theatre (BFKBT). Some of the vaudeville entertainers who appeared at the theatre under Keith included the Marx Brothers; comedian and singer Sophie Tucker; Ken Murray and his wife Charlotte LaRose; actresses Elsie Janis, Mrs. Leslie Carter, Valeska Suratt and Ione Bright; actor Berton Churchill in a Shakespeare act; minstrel show entertainer Eddie Leonard; female impersonator Julian Eltinge; and Mayme Remington and her all-black cast tap dancing troupe. The theatre was also occasionally used by touring stock theatre companies for performances of plays and musical theatre.

title: RKO Bushwick Theatre
text: By 1925 the BFKBT was offering screenings of silent films in addition to live entertainment. The theatre continued to operate as BFKBT until 1929 when it became the RKOBT; beginning in February of that year with a screening of the film Annapolis in conjunction a live variety theatre show. Live vaudeville entertainments paired with film screening continued into the 1930s with performers like opera singer Everett Marshall and the comic musical duo Arren and Broderick. The RKOBT continued to operate as a movie theatre until closing in 1969. The building was soon after converted into a church; becoming the Pilgrim Baptist Church. It was a church for a relatively short period in the 1970s.

title: Battle of Waj
text: From 1529 to 1543, the jihad led by Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi brought the Christian kingdom close to collapse, according to the introduction to the standard translation of Gelawdewos's chronicle. Waj was one of the first of the south-western provinces to be drawn into the invasion. Gelawdewos succeeded his father Lebna Dengel in 1540 at about the age of eighteen. A Portuguese contingent of 400 men under Cristóvão da Gama arrived in 1541 to support him; after it was defeated at the Battle of Wofla in August 1542, the survivors joined Gelawdewos's army, and in 1543 Ahmad was killed at Wayna Daga.

title: Battle of Waj
text: It was during the second month of the Ethiopian year that Gelawdewos came to Waj after a long march. On hearing about this, Abbas vacated his territories and went to meet him, accompanied by his chiefs and soldiers. According to the translator, the campaign took place in October 1544. Aregay explains Abbas's actions as a strategy to stop the emperor in case he marched into Bali and Dawaro, and as an act of desperation to save the Muslims of these provinces, not a miscalculation of his own power. In his account, Abbas's forces were fewer in number, and many of the able commanders and horsemen who had served Ahmad had already been killed in earlier battles.

title: Battle of Waj
text: King Gälawdewos arrived in the land of Wäǧ after many journeys. When he heard this, Wazir Abbas set out from the land that he inhabited with all his chiefs and his troops rushing out like a furious dog in a hurry to bite and exultation blowing the horn like a strong horse. But King Gälawdewos was waiting to receive him calmly as the bridegroom is used to receive. In fact, his steadfast heart was solidly trusted to God, he was never disturbed for ever until he saw in his enemies. Their confrontation took place in the day at which God, be praised his name, decided. And He gave a crown for King Gälawdewos to win and he went out and he won. Abbas and the whole of his commanders fell by the iron (sword).

title: Scripture cake
text: Scripture cake may have originated in Britain in 18th century. These recipes often feature in America in community cookbooks, sometimes under the names bible cake, scriptural cake, or Old Testament cake. From the late 19th through early 20th century, recipes for scripture cakes were ubiquitous in church community cookbooks across the country, appearing in more than half of the books produced in the period in the US. At church fairs during the period, slices of scripture cakes with their recipes were often sold to raise money. Scripture cakes continued to appear widely during the second half of the 20th century, particularly in the southern US. Scripture cakes are still made in the US in churches, both by children at Sunday school and adults in groups. They are prominent in the cookbooks of African-American authors. Outside of the US, recipes for scripture cake have appeared in cookbooks in Canada and the UK.

title: Karl Mokaraka
text: Mokaraka stood at the 2023 New Zealand general election for Vision NZ, contesting the Panmure-Ōtāhuhu electorate. At the Ōtara Markets in August, he led a protest against Labour leader Chris Hipkins. Later that same month, Mokaraka heckled Prime Minister Christopher Luxon from behind a fence, while Luxon was giving a media briefing in Pakuranga. Mokaraka's back-and-forth exchange with Luxon, which lasted for several minutes, resulted in memes on social media. After another heckling of David Seymour at ACT's campaign launch, Mokaraka began to be described as a serial heckler, a label he rejects. Mokaraka told The New Zealand Herald that he was motivated to heckle at political events to represent whānau without a voice.

title: Watchers of Time
text: But Rutledge is unconvinced. Father James had been struck from behind, as if someone had been waiting in ambush. And more valuable items had been left untouched, which spoke against burglary being the motive. Rutledge begins to dig into the past of Father James and discovers that Father James had been obsessed with the 1912 sinking of the Titanic, collecting clippings and annotating photographs and lists of both of the survivors and those who had drowned. This was the second time that Rutledge had recently heard the name Titanic, for it had come up in conversation that Lord Sedgewick's daughter-in-law, Virginia, fleeing from her marriage to the lord's older son some seven years ago, had booked passage on the Titanic to return to her American family, and had gone down with the ship. But as Father James' clippings show, her name was originally not on the passenger list, but only appeared a few days after the tragedy. Rutledge also discovers that while Virginia had been beautiful, she had also been developmentally handicapped, possessing the mental acuity of a 7-year old. The Sedgewick family had not realized this until after the marriage, arranged with Virginia's American family, had taken place. The Sedgewicks, unwilling to let anyone else in British high society know about this, isolated her. Eventually Virginia had slipped away from the Sedgewick chauffeur during a shopping trip, and apparently made her way to Southampton, where she bought passage on the Titanic.

title: Watchers of Time
text: Publishers Weekly thought the action was too slow, calling the novel "tiresomely paced ... The book's overall theme is a compelling one: questions of guilt and responsibility after the debacle that was WWI. But the tangle of motives and intrigue that surrounds the priest's murder is too complex (and, ultimately, too trivial) to support such a theme." The review concluded, "Like previous entries in this series, this one is psychologically astute, but the narrative becomes too bogged down with the author's desire to portray postwar English village life and too weighted with the enormity of its themes."

title: The Pines, Brighton
text: The Pines, Brighton was constructed in 1866 by local prolific builder and dairyman William Durrant on 4 hectares (10 acres) he owned in the Brighton Estate, between Middle and Outer Crescent, where he built seven cottages. The Pines was the second in a sequence of larger concrete houses built by Durrant and the first occupant was the squatter, Frank W. Desailly. By 1872 The Pines was used as a school known as Brighton College and it appears that a timber addition was constructed at the rear for this purpose. This school was initially conducted by John MacVean, then John Batten until 1881, and finally Arthur Backhouse until c. 1883.

title: The Pines, Brighton
text: The Pines, Brighton is a concrete house with a hipped slate roof and brick and timber sections at the rear. It is a mid-Victorian Italianate villa with rendered walls which are lightly scribed to imitate ashlar construction. It has moulded chimney caps, quoined front corners, a central front door and tall paired double hung windows on either side. A concave roofed front verandah was modified with a replacement frame, concrete floor, and turned posts. The eaves have an unusual continuous rendered under-mould. The interior of the main house has a timber floor, plastered walls and ceilings, deep cornices and deep timber window reveals. At the rear of the main house are two sections, one of brick construction and a later addition to the west is of timber construction. To the rear of the property are two concrete outbuildings with corrugated iron roofs. It is recorded that the concrete used to form the walls of the house and outbuildings consisted of lime binding sand and stones from the nearby foreshore. This was rammed in layers before a rendered finish was applied.

title: Lin Yuying
text: In the spring of 1923, Lin returned to Changsha as a technician and party branch secretary at the Wangluyuan Weaving Factory. On 28 May, he led a strike by the city's rickshaw pullers against an increase in the fees charged by vehicle owners, which succeeded on 5 June. On 1 June, he led rickshaw pullers in a demonstration in Changsha protesting against the killing of Chinese civilians by Japanese sailors. In the autumn, he became business manager and party branch secretary of the Anyuan Railway and Mining Workers' Consumer Cooperative and joined the work of the CCP's Anyuan district committee. On 1 May 1924, he served as chief marshal at the opening of the new building of the Anyuan Railway and Mining Workers' Club. He then travelled to the Soviet Union and, after arriving in Moscow at the end of October 1924, studied at the Communist University of the Toilers of the East.

title: Lin Yuying
text: Lin was recalled to China in May 1925 and worked for the CCP's Shanghai committee. That year, he joined the party group of the Shanghai General Labour Union and became secretary of the CCP's Yangshupu section committee. On 6 December 1925, he took part in a mass rally organised by the union and other groups on Qingyun Road against Duan Qirui and the Fengtian clique. While leading the marchers, he was seriously injured in a clash with soldiers and police, and a head wound left him with lasting migraines. In 1926, he served as secretary of the Yangshupu and then the Caojiadu section committees, and in April he became a member of the CCP's Shanghai district committee.

title: Lin Yuying
text: In January 1927, Lin went to Hankou, where he served as an adjutant and head of a special detachment of the military commission of the Wuhan Nationalist Government. During the July 1927 break between the Wuhan government and the communists, he ran a furniture shop that served as a secret liaison point for the party. In September 1927, on the orders of the CCP's Hubei committee, he, Wang Juexin and Shi Bingqian formed the party's East Hubei Special Committee. The committee led Autumn Harvest Uprisings in Daye, Yangxin and Echeng, which failed. He then served as secretary of the CCP's Qiaokou district committee and, from October, as secretary of the Wuchang municipal workers' committee.

title: Granite B
text: The difference from the old Tonghab camouflage is based on digital pixels. The background for the issuance of this new combat uniform is that U.S. military requests for uniform improvements began in 2004, and the project got on track in earnest when the Department of Defense accepted the plan to improve the new combat uniform in May 2009. At that time, the United States had already introduced ACU combat uniforms produced using digital pixels such as Universal Camouflage Pattern. For landscape and environment context, there were three test types: granite, pine, and rock, and the granite pattern, which is very common in the terrain of the Korean Peninsula, was finally selected. Unlike the existing uniform, the new combat uniform also enhanced the functionality of the uniform itself and was manufactured using advanced fibers. This Granite B combat uniforms began to be issued to the Army, Navy, and Air Force starting in 2014.

title: Granite B
text: During the parade on January 14, 2021, the Korea People's Army Ground Forces wore digital camouflage uniforms and combat boots similar to the desert-colored combat boots that the Republic of Korea Army recently began issuing. The shape and material of the pockets match the initial type of the Republic of Korea Armed Forces standard combat uniform, and the pattern is also in the form of a color inversion. There was also an article that said some Korean-Chinese merchants were involved in leaking Korean military camouflage patterns. However, until first quarter of 2022, these camouflage been provided to strategic forces and military parade units actively mobilized for propaganda. But in 2026, North Korean military wore digital camouflage uniform, similar to Granite B and EMR camouflage.

title: Sutton Monro
text: Monro attended the Philips Andover Academy and Cambridge High and Latin School, followed by Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where he graduated with a bachelor's degree from the Department of Business and Engineering Administration in 1942. He was enlisted in the US Navy during war times and fought in World War II. After the war, he taught mathematics at the University of Maine at Orono from 1946 to 1948. Monro then enrolled himself at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in the fall of 1948 to pursue a doctoral study in statistics. Originally, he was interested in working under Harold Hotelling, but after talking to multiple other faculties, in 1949, he decided to work with a newer faculty member, Herbert Robbins, as his supervisor for a sequential analysis problem Monro proposed. Robbins was about a year younger than Monro, during the next years, Monro had a personal conflict with Robbins when he was made aware that Robbins was communicating with Jacob Wolfowitz and Jack Kiefer, then at Columbia University, about the results he was working on. Robbins published the work in September 1951, before Monro finished his Ph.D. (now called the Robbins-Monro algorithm), a year before Kiefer and Wolfowitz, who came to a more general version. The rule at the time at University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill prevented students to publish their doctoral work before being awarded their degree. This means that Monro never received his Ph.D.

title: Sinderlyn
text: Sniper framed Sinderlyn as a way of expanding without diluting his main label. He told SLUG Magazine in 2015: "Our roster on Captured Tracks is full, so I developed Sinderlyn as a way to start working with more artists and also not dilute Captured Tracks by signing a ton of bands to it. It's not a sub-label [to Captured Tracks]; it's a sister label." By 2017 the label was also being used for artists who had come through major-label deals; Sniper told Forbes that year that Sinderlyn was "a sister label solely for established artists coming out of the major label process", citing the signing of Cults as an example.

title: AEW Fright Night (2026)
text: The 2026 Fright Night was a two-part professional wrestling television special produced by All Elite Wrestling (AEW). It is the third annual Fright Night event and took place on October 28, 2026 at the Chaifetz Arena in St. Louis, Missouri, encompassing the broadcasts of Wednesday Night Dynamite and Saturday Night Collision. Dynamite aired live on October 28 on TBS in the United States, while Collision was taped that same day and aired on tape delay on October 31 on TNT, also in the United States; this was the first time that the event is held as a two-part event. Both shows were simulcast on the streaming service HBO Max.

title: AEW Fright Night (2026)
text: Fright Night is an annual professional wrestling television special produced by the American promotion All Elite Wrestling (AEW) since 2024. Until 2025, the event aired as a Halloween-themed special episode of the company's flagship weekly program, Wednesday Night Dynamite, however, on August 24, 2026, AEW announced that the 2026 edition of Fright Night would take place on October 28, 2026, at the Chaifetz Arena in St. Louis as a two-part event, encompassing a live edition of Dynamite airing on TBS, and a taped edition of Saturday Night Collision airing on TNT on October 28, 2026, marking the first time that the event would take place as a two-part event. Both events would also simulcast on the streaming service HBO Max in the United States.

title: 1918 Grande Prairie murders
text: Both Joseph and Stanley were born in the Waterloo Region of Ontario. Before moving to Alberta in 1913, Joseph was a bookkeeper. Stanley, who was suffering from kidney problems, worked for the Grand Trunk Pacific Railway in Vancouver until March 1918, when he joined his uncle in Alberta. Joseph, who was unmarried, was known as a respected and quiet man, while a close friend of Stanley's described him as "a man who attended strictly to his own business at all times." Neither was known to be on bad terms with anyone or each other, nor were they believed to possess notable sums of money by the police.

title: 1918 Grande Prairie murders
text: Patten's business partner, Charles Zimmer, also a farmer and trapper, came from a Lithuanian background. He had moved to the area in 1910, and wore dentures containing a distinctive gold tooth. Reporting on the crime contains several variations of his name, including Zimmner and Zermenter. Patten and Zimmer had also partnered with James Wuwand (also known as John), who was a newcomer to Canada from Russia. Known as a kindly, harmless man of short stature, locals affectionately called him "John the Russian". He had worked at a livery and in sales. Known variations of his name include Unward and Wudwud.

title: 1918 Grande Prairie murders
text: Frank Peter Parzychowski (also recorded as Parzychowsky) was an ethnic Ruthenian from Poland who worked as a blacksmith. At one point, he was a priest within the Greek Catholic Church, and was known to be well-travelled. He had emigrated to Canada by 1910 after living in North Dakota for 20 years and was married to a woman named Rose, who was also known as "Rosie". In 1911, he participated in a human interest story on his travels for the Evening Journal, wherein he described Grande Prairie as the best place "in the world". He died on June 18 or 19, 1918. Originally buried in the Mission Cemetery near Bear Creek, his grave was moved to the City of Grande Prairie Cemetery in 1966.

title: Fred C. Leone
text: Leone earned his BA (1942) from Manhattan College (now Manhattan University), his MS (1943) from Georgetown University and his PhD in statistics from Purdue University (1949). His PhD thesis, written under the tutelage of Irving W. Burr, was titled Some Extensions Of Bayes Theorem. After serving in the United States Navy during World War II, he became an instructor at Case Institute of Technology, rising to the rank of professor in 1964. In 1967, Leone joined the faculty of the Department of Statistics, University of Iowa. In 1973, he left academia and became executive director of the American Statistical Association, where he remained until his retirement in 1988.

title: VFL Park Superboard
text: Waverley Park hosted its final AFL match in 1999, with the last competitive senior football match (the 2000 VFL Grand Final) played at the venue on 27 August 2000. After this, Waverley Park was not maintained, with vandals breaking into the site and damaging the facilities. Only the Sir Kenneth Luke Stand and the members' stand mural were listed on the Victorian Heritage Register, with the stadium demolished starting on 11 December 2002. The Superboard was one of the last elements to be removed of the ground, with bulldozers first flattening the outer lower stands located around the scoreboard. No elements of the Superboard were believed to have been saved; Erb said "it all went to the tip" and he did not keep any souvenirs.
